facts.f: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was called the 'Missile Man of India'.
facts.e: He was a scientist who later became India's 11th President.

facts.f: Mother Teresa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
facts.e: She spent most of her life caring for the poor and sick in Kolkata.

facts.f: Savitribai Phule is remembered as India's first woman teacher.
facts.e: In 1848, she and Jyotirao Phule started a school for girls in Pune.

facts.f: Swami Vivekananda gave a famous speech at Chicago in 1893.
facts.e: He began with 'Sisters and Brothers of America'. His birthday, 12 January, is National Youth Day.

facts.f: Dr B. R. Ambedkar earned doctorates from Columbia University and the London School of Economics.
facts.e: He worked all his life for equality and the rights of the oppressed.

facts.f: Sarojini Naidu became the first woman Governor of an Indian state in 1947.
facts.e: She was Governor of the United Provinces, now Uttar Pradesh.

facts.f: Indira Gandhi was India's first woman Prime Minister.
facts.e: She first became Prime Minister in 1966.

facts.f: Pratibha Patil was India's first woman President.
facts.e: She was President from 2007 to 2012.

facts.f: Kiran Bedi became India's first woman IPS officer in 1972.
facts.e: IPS stands for Indian Police Service.

facts.f: Anandibai Joshi was one of the first Indian women to earn a degree in Western medicine, in 1886.
facts.e: She studied in the United States at a time when few women anywhere could become doctors.

facts.f: Satyendra Nath Bose's ideas about particles of light were developed further by Albert Einstein.
facts.e: A whole family of particles, called bosons, is named after him.

facts.f: Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect, not for relativity.
facts.e: The photoelectric effect is how light can knock electrons out of metal.

facts.f: Stephen Hawking was a physicist who studied black holes and the Universe.
facts.e: He had a disease that slowly paralysed him, and he spoke using a computer voice.

facts.f: Helen Keller became deaf and blind as a baby, but grew up to be an author and speaker.
facts.e: Her teacher, Anne Sullivan, taught her words by spelling them into her hand.

facts.f: Florence Nightingale is known as the founder of modern nursing.
facts.e: She was called 'The Lady with the Lamp' because she checked on wounded soldiers at night.

facts.f: Martin Luther King Jr. gave his famous 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963.
facts.e: He worked for equal rights through peaceful protest and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.

facts.f: Mahatma Gandhi led India's freedom struggle through non-violence.
facts.e: He called his method satyagraha, which means holding firmly to truth.

facts.f: Raja Ram Mohan Roy worked to end the practice of sati.
facts.e: He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 and supported education for all.

facts.f: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar fought for the right of widows to remarry.
facts.e: The Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 thanks to his efforts.

facts.f: Nikola Tesla developed the alternating current (AC) electrical system.
facts.e: The electricity in our homes is AC.

facts.f: Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean, in 1932.
facts.e: She disappeared in 1937 while trying to fly around the world.

facts.f: Arunima Sinha was the first female amputee to climb Mount Everest, in 2013.
facts.e: She climbed with an artificial leg after losing her leg in an accident.

facts.f: Verghese Kurien is called the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India.
facts.e: His Operation Flood made India the world's largest milk producer. National Milk Day, 26 November, is his birthday.

facts.f: M. S. Swaminathan is called the 'Father of the Green Revolution' in India.
facts.e: He helped India grow much more wheat and rice.

facts.f: E. Sreedharan is known as the 'Metro Man' of India.
facts.e: He led the building of the Konkan Railway and the Delhi Metro.

facts.f: Asked how India looked from space, Rakesh Sharma replied, 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'.
facts.e: It means 'better than the whole world', from a famous poem by Muhammad Iqbal.

facts.f: Jamsetji Tata founded the Tata Group and is called the father of Indian industry.
facts.e: He dreamed of a steel plant, a science institute and a grand hotel for India.

facts.f: Malala Yousafzai became the youngest Nobel Prize winner in 2014, at age 17.
facts.e: She stood up for every girl's right to go to school.

facts.f: Kailash Satyarthi shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai.
facts.e: He has worked to free children from child labour.

facts.f: Har Gobind Khorana won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1968.
facts.e: He helped explain how the genetic code works.

facts.f: Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1998.
facts.e: He studied poverty, famine and well-being.

facts.f: Lata Mangeshkar was one of India's most loved singers.
facts.e: She sang thousands of songs and received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

facts.f: Jane Goodall spent decades studying chimpanzees in the wild.
facts.e: She discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools.

facts.f: Salim Ali is known as the 'Birdman of India'.
facts.e: He studied and wrote about Indian birds for over 60 years.

facts.f: Tipu Sultan of Mysore used iron-cased rockets in battle against the British.
facts.e: These rockets inspired later rocket designs in Britain.

facts.f: Anna Chandy became India's first woman judge in 1937.
facts.e: She later became the first woman judge of a High Court in India.

facts.f: Fathima Beevi became the first woman judge of India's Supreme Court in 1989.
facts.e: She later served as Governor of Tamil Nadu.

facts.f: Neerja Bhanot was a flight attendant who saved many passengers during a hijacking in 1986.
facts.e: She was the youngest person to receive the Ashoka Chakra, India's highest peacetime award for bravery.

facts.f: Thomas Edison held more than 1,000 patents in the United States.
facts.e: His inventions include the phonograph, which recorded and played sound.

facts.f: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray photographs helped reveal the double-helix shape of DNA.
facts.e: Her famous 'Photo 51' was taken in 1952.

facts.f: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, in 1963.
facts.e: She orbited Earth 48 times in nearly three days.

facts.f: Louis Braille lost his sight as a small child and invented Braille as a teenager.
facts.e: He developed his reading system at the age of 15.
